competency_fulfillment.rationale: The sample set fully satisfies the MATATAG learning competency 'Add numbers with sums up to 10 000, with and without regrouping.' by assessing addition across 2-digit, 3-digit, and 4-digit addends with sums up to 10,000, as demonstrated in 4-digit problems like "What is 9021 + 757?" and "7361 + 2510 = 9871. True or False?", 3-digit problems like "What is 114 + 10?", and identity property addition like "What is 146 + 0?".

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The items span a comprehensive range of representations and cognitive modalities including direct arithmetic equations ("110 + 45 = ___"), number line models ("Show 90 + 108 on the number line." and "The dot is at 150 and it moves forward 7 numbers. Starting from 150, just count up 7 numbers. Which number will the dot land on?"), part-part-whole reasoning ("The two parts are 10 and 115. What is the sum?"), and contextual word problems ("Pia has 208 water bowls. A friend has 0 water bowls. If they put all their water bowls together, how many water bowls do they have in all?").

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The reading level, structural framing, and question complexity are well-calibrated for Grade 3 Quarter 2 students. Item prompts are concise and clear, avoiding extraneous cognitive load or non-target vocabulary, as seen in "The two parts are 9093 and 700. What is the sum?" and "What is 120 + 72?".

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The generator produces a diverse array of response formats and prompt variants, spanning standard multiple-choice ("What is 127 + 30?"), cloze fill-in ("143 + 0 = ___"), truth verification ("44 + 0 = 54. True or False?"), interactive number line placement ("Show 114 + 130 on the number line."), and part-whole sum identification ("The two parts are 9093 and 700. What is the sum?").

competency_alignment.rationale: All generated items directly assess whole number addition within the MATATAG curriculum bounds for this competency without introducing out-of-scope operations such as multiplication or division. Questions like "What is 130 + 11?" and "240 + 4 = ___" align precisely with the learning standard.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The numerical values strictly conform to the Grade 3 Quarter 2 scale, spanning from 2- and 3-digit operations ("109 + 30 = ___") up to large 4-digit sums approaching 10 000 such as "7361 + 2510 = 9871. True or False?" (sum 9871) and "The two parts are 9093 and 700. What is the sum?" (sum 9793), without exceeding the 10 000 ceiling.
